A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MINT research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendix A. Pages 2–18 have identical extracted text and rendered content; first-page differences concern author order and version/date information.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MiniGrid, Atari Pacman, and NVIDIA Isaac in Tables 1–3, plus model comparisons and uncertainty analysis in Appendix Tables 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The UA-DQN training, symbolic tree expansion, LLM query curation and updating, and Isaac planning adaptation are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 in Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MiniGrid uncertain-object scenarios, modified Atari Pacman environment, and Isaac warehouse search-and-rescue tasks. Appendix A.4 retains identical coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GPT-4o, o3-mini, o3, DQN, and PPO in MiniGrid; DQN, PPO, and Query-A in Atari; and the three pure-LLM baselines in Isaac.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.3–A.4 retain the same observation and preprocessing procedures, metrics, model configurations, training settings, and query limits. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The limited-versus-standard MINT comparisons, within-MINT LLM comparison in Table 5, and uncertainty decline analysis in Table 6 are identical. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state 100 evaluation runs per environment, five training seeds for methods involving training, and reporting of averages and standard deviations. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match, including Tables 1–3 and 5–6. For example, standard MINT's Atari return remains 434.9 ± 32.1 in Table 2, and Table 6 retains identical uncertainty trajectories.

T1.justification: The MDP-family definitions, mathematical reasoning in Section 4.3, Lemmas 4.2–4.3, Theorem 4.4, and all derivations and proofs in Appendix A.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about MINT's novelty, theoretical return guarantees, and near-expert planning performance with few queries.

C2.justification: The interpretations of LLM conservatism, knowledge reuse through queries, uncertainty reduction, and stronger LLMs' limited benefits and time costs are unchanged. No substantive qualification or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Appendix pseudocode, Table 4 hyperparameters, prompt Listings 1–3, environment implementation details, and hardware disclosures are identical. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and statements positioning MINT relative to prior planning, human-in-the-loop, and neuro-symbolic methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The author order changes from Zeyu Fang, Tian Lan, Mahdi Imani to Zeyu Fang, Mahdi Imani, Tian Lan. The preprint date changes from February 6 to May 5, 2026, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–6 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the first-page edits only replace author and date/version text.

improvement.justification: v2 changes author order and first-page version/date information while retaining the same scientific text, proofs, experiments, appendix details, and visual presentation. These administrative edits establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
